title: Large personal CPC, C64, BBC and Atari ST discovery
summary: Personally screen 330 candidate URLs and add 30 projects; record five exclusions and one specific template-versus-port deferral.
notes: All discovery research and publication performed by the root assistant, without a research worker, PR or branch. Five fresh searches plus three C64 tooling follow-ups were screened against current main. Primary source, build recipes and implementation-stage distinctions were inspected. A README-directed dev branch supplied the Skweek prototype; root URL is retained. Historical source ports, machine-code reconstructions, native homebrew, format tools and source-only prototypes are distinguished. BBC Quake requires an ARM coprocessor; GB2CPC is uncompiled early-alpha compatibility work, Karl is extraction rather than a finished TIC-80 port, and AYMax engine source is not included. Creator-documented Feud patches are binary-only releases, not source reconstruction. No upstream executable, ROM, firmware, network client or hardware operation was run. Large/legacy-encoded source is linked at immutable revisions where embedding would not be lossless. No development-AI inference from an agent instruction file alone.

sources.reason: Author distributes documented invincibility/no-enemy-healing variants, plus an Atari item-pickup fix.
Substantive BASIC listing contains stage, ammo, scoring and screen logic with native routine calls.
CPCTelera implementation has movement, levels, drawing and collision logic.
Extracts packed level nibbles and CPC sprite pixel data from existing assembly/data listings.
Early GBDK-style API and Mode-1 tile/palette conversion library, with virtual OAM and a small moving-sprite example.
The advertised dev branch contains actual PaperScript grid/player/enemy/win-state logic; default branch contains only a pointer to dev.
Readable BASIC implementation and word database recreate a Fallout-style word-matching terminal puzzle.
Spanish choose-your-own-adventure runtime and Java narrative compiler generate indexed C text/options tables.
Converts Toby Nelson’s annotated ACME MOS disassembly to BeebAsm and supplies original/optimized conditional builds with a revised line editor.
Common editor routines and variables shared by BBC/Master/6502-coprocessor/C64 Universe Editor builds.
WinQuake-derived engine adapted to BBC ADFS naming, Tube video and optional VideoNULA/RGB2HDMI/Pi framebuffer output.
Arduino sketches test DRAM/PLA/ROM chips and include a cartridge-dump routine plus timing fixtures.
Converts BASIC text to linked tokenized PRG lines and decodes PRG back to text.
Generic CRT header/launcher and build recipe package a PRG using Exomizer and 64tass.
Visual waveform/sample parsing and TAP editing support restoration of recorded cassette audio.
Traverses magazine disk data and decompresses text/graphics into reformatted output.
Multicolor bitmap optimizer converts Koala, bitmap, screen and color RAM representations; inspected palette assignment implementation.
Native joystick-controlled SID register/voice parameter editor with screen/input/sound source modules.
Host editor assigns per-character values over a multicolor image and exports1000-byte40×25 screen maps; includes speedcode example.
Historical Final TAP source has format-specific loader scanners, cleaning, CRC and extraction routines with tape-format documentation.
Parses XML boot/file manifests into banked cartridge and EasyFS directory data.
Fluent instruction API and simulator support generation and testing of C64-oriented6502/6510 programs, including SID/MIDI utilities.
Substantial browser game and level editor reconstruct the C64 Survivor experience with custom movement/collision/rendering code.
Shared C HTTP/transport engine powers a NextZXOS dot command and library for entity state and service calls.
Converts TAYM tracks and wraps prebuilt AYMax engines in Spectrum128K tape/snapshot loaders; wrapper assembly and format tooling are source available.
Disassembly-derived C accessory and patched assembly fix timing, window lifecycle and multitasking issues; Plus adds resizing and other extensions.
Converts prepared GIF frames into four-part multicolor sprites with explicit palette mapping and a native demonstration.
Hotkey-driven screen-memory dump with sequential filenames; readable assembler listing accompanies original tool artifacts.
Audio preparation/quantization and native players export packed4-bit digis, PRGs, streaming EasyFlash and MSSIAH WAV; real pipeline and boot assembly inspected.
Only a README announces an OLAF TIC-80 port; no implementation or original creator release is available here.
Root contains only a short README and license, with no game source or release artifact to qualify.
README explicitly describes tools collected from the internet; tree provides bundled diagnostics rather than distinct source or analysis contribution.
GitHub reports an empty repository; palette announcement has no inspectable implementation.
Inspected program is a generic Harfang scene/FPS-camera and ImGui demonstration. Project-specific models alone do not establish the advertised 3D Fight gameplay reconstruction.

Repository description advertises Cho Ren Sa but README, app descriptor and current source remain a generic framebuffer/demo template. Compare against md-framebuffer-template and inspect any later game-specific branch before asserting a distinct Cho Ren Sa port; RP2040 execution must not be presented as native ST game logic.
